kaigo-atomic-grooming-figure.heading: What shaving and nail diagrams establish
paragraphs: Facial hair relates to appearance and preferences, so first ask how the person wants it arranged. Check skin, equipment and product instructions, explain the actions and obtain consent. Do not impose a shape staff consider tidy.

The textbook’s electric-shaver figure gives an example of applying the blade close to a right angle while smoothing skin wrinkles. It does not mean pressing hard to finish faster. A remembered angle does not apply automatically to different blades or heads; check that product’s method.

Check shaved areas to avoid missing hair or unnecessarily repeating the same spot. Also monitor skin and sensation. Finishing moisturizers must suit skin, wishes and plan; a textbook lotion example is not an instruction to use one product for everyone.

The nail diagram calls a shaped-tip example square-off and contrasts deep cutting and diagonal bias cutting. Nail clippers and files are tools with different roles. Long or sharp nails can injure skin, and dirt collects around nails. The purpose is cleanliness and protection, not cutting more deeply for greater cleanliness. Knowing diagram terms does not authorize treatment of abnormal nails.

Nail condition can reflect health, so inspect nails and surrounding skin rather than length alone. Tell healthcare professionals about pain, redness, swelling or other abnormalities and check methods without diagnosing from appearance. Softer nails after bathing or a person’s urgency do not authorize independent care of abnormal nails. Smooth sharp edges afterward with a file or similar tool within the appropriate scope.

[Learning example] Someone applies a remembered angle from an old shaver to a new one. First check the model, instructions, skin and wishes. Understanding a diagram differs from establishing safe-use conditions for this device and person.

This teaches diagram and terminology meanings and reasons for assistance. Actual care follows condition, the individual care plan, product instructions and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar actions from words or pictures alone or record unchecked results.

kaigo-atomic-bed-wash-figures.heading: Connect bed-bath areas, movements and warmth
paragraphs: A bed bath cleans with warm towels or suitable products when bathing or showering is unsuitable, for example. The source also discusses stimulation of circulation and muscles, but this does not mean stronger rubbing is better. Adapt to skin and reactions. Whole-body and partial care differ; check the area desired and suitable method rather than assuming whole-body consent.

Prepare separate clean and used supplies. Handle face, arms, chest and abdomen, back and legs area by area. Treat genital care separately with contamination and consent scope in mind. Beyond memorized order, the aims are preventing spread of contamination, maintaining warmth and limiting exposure. Check methods if they do not suit individual conditions.

The facial example starts around the eyes and includes behind the ears and neck. Circular chest movements and movements along back muscles illustrate locations and directions. Do not treat shoulder-area transverse lines, circular chest/abdomen/buttock lines and long back/side lines as identical movement instructions.

Limb figures show broad wiping movements using joints as boundaries, not cleaning only around joints. The source’s steady-pressure description does not prescribe identical force for everyone. Avoid strong friction on thin, injured or painful skin; check reactions, skin and range of movement. Arrows alone do not determine force or repetitions.

Check and remove cleanser residue because it may cause itching. Moisture promotes heat loss, so dry each area promptly after cleaning and cover while working elsewhere. Exposing and wetting the whole body before drying everything does not necessarily protect warmth and embarrassment equally well.

Because bed-bath water cools, the source gives an example of preparing water warmer than bathwater and keeping adjustment water available. Container water, wet towel and skin-contact temperature are not identical conditions. Check suitable temperature during use as well as preparation through methods matching the plan and equipment. Never apply hot adjustment water directly or carry it over the person. Do not reinterpret this as ‘hotter is better.’

[Learning example] The person wants only their arms wiped. Whole-body supplies do not extend assistance scope. Confirm the area and method and separately review preparation, wiping, cleanser-residue checks, drying and covering with their purposes and actual results.

This teaches diagram and terminology meanings and reasons for assistance. Actual care follows condition, the individual care plan, product instructions and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar actions from words or pictures alone or record unchecked results.

kaigo-atomic-adl-iadl.heading: Mobility connects daily actions and choices
paragraphs: For mobility support, ask what the person wants to do at the destination, not only where to go. Eating, toileting, bathing and relationships all involve movement. Accessible activity ranges relate to physical and mental functions and participation.

ADL includes basic daily actions such as eating, changing, bathing, toileting and mobility. IADL includes shopping, managing money, laundry and transport or communication use supporting home and community life. Category names do not establish overall personal ability.

Cooking preparation, cleaning, laundry, clothing organization, shopping and communication differ by habits and values even under shared activity names. Check what the person decides and can do, then match help to needs. One independent ADL does not prove every IADL ability.

[Learning example] A person needs wheelchair-mobility help but manages their budget and choices independently. Mobility limits do not transfer every shopping decision to family. Check intentions and managed tasks, considering help such as reaching the shop separately.

This teaches diagram and terminology meanings and reasons for assistance. Actual care follows condition, the individual care plan, product instructions and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar actions from words or pictures alone or record unchecked results.

kaigo-atomic-posture-names.heading: Check body-position names with actual support
paragraphs: Standing, sitting and lying are distinct positions. Chair sitting, sitting at the bed edge with legs lowered and long sitting with legs extended have different support surfaces and foot positions. A sitting label alone does not establish equal stability.

Supine means lying on the back, side-lying means on one side and prone means face down. Right side-lying places the person’s right side down, not right as seen by a facing worker. Check the body side contacting support, not only face direction.

Body position describes placement or posture; repositioning is changing it. Posture describes the body’s arrangement. Distinguish current state from transition in expressions such as remaining at the bed edge, moving into chair sitting or moving to standing.

The supine example supports the body over a broad surface, but that alone does not make it best for everyone. Pain, breathing, pressure and wishes affect suitable support. Names such as Fowler’s or semi-Fowler’s do not prescribe one bed angle for everyone.

Side-lying examples use cushions in front of the chest, beneath the lower leg or between legs. The semi-sitting example raises the bed’s leg section or supports under the knees with a cushion if that section cannot be adjusted. The aim is stability and avoidance of unnecessary pressure or sliding. Check locations, thickness and skin contact against personal and equipment conditions.

[Learning example] ‘Placed a pillow’ does not establish what was supported or whether comfort improved. Record the supported area and position, pain and breathing, the person’s own words and confirmed results after adjustment. A pillow’s presence is not confirmed comfort.

This teaches diagram and terminology meanings and reasons for assistance. Actual care follows condition, the individual care plan, product instructions and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar actions from words or pictures alone or record unchecked results.

kaigo-atomic-disuse.heading: Check inactivity and pressure risks separately
paragraphs: Prolonged rest or reduced activity can cause muscle wasting, restricted joint movement and reduced bone, sensory or mental functions. These are studied as disuse syndrome. Time lying down alone does not determine every individual function.

Cardiorespiratory function, pressure regulation, internal organs, nutrition and activity ability can also be affected. The diagram includes orthostatic hypotension, a pressure drop on standing. Observe and report dizziness, palpitations or breathlessness when rising, but do not attribute new symptoms solely to inactivity; arrange needed assessment.

Pressure injuries involve continued pressure, such as over bony prominences, impairing blood flow. Check contact and skin at areas appropriate to posture, including back of head, shoulder blades, elbows, sacrum/buttocks and heels. One checked area or posture does not establish no risk elsewhere.

Review bedding wrinkles, friction and sliding together with pressure. Smoothing wrinkles matters but does not remove prolonged pressure on one site. Consider movement ability, support surfaces, skin, activity and nutrition together.

Combine appropriate activity, getting out of bed, repositioning, pressure relief and nutrition under individual assessment and plan. One schedule for everyone does not complete checks; observe condition and responses afterward. Changing or cleaning offers skin-observation opportunities. Report redness or other changes to healthcare professionals without waiting for a wound.

The textbook’s back-release example after raising the upper body illustrates relieving skin shear. Understanding its purpose does not authorize independently pulling or lifting the person. Check suitable equipment, method and helpers and use facility-trained techniques.

[Learning example] Sheets are smooth, but the heel remains pressed on one spot for a long time. No wrinkles does not mean no pressure-injury risk. Check heel contact, skin and sensation and the planned support and reporting requirements.

This teaches diagram and terminology meanings and reasons for assistance. Actual care follows condition, the individual care plan, product instructions and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar actions from words or pictures alone or record unchecked results.

kaigo-atomic-movement-devices.heading: Distinguish equipment purposes and component roles
paragraphs: Canes, walkers and lifts have different support purposes and conditions. T-handled canes are light and easy to handle; multipoint canes have broader support bases. The source gives multipoint examples with reduced leg stability or strength, but those conditions alone do not establish suitability. Walkers also broaden support, yet base size does not rank one aid best for everyone. Check movement, location, device and professional assessment together.

Lifts include ceiling-track and mobile floor types for supporting transfers. Appropriate correct use can reduce burdens on both person and worker. Model-name knowledge does not establish operating ability; check personal condition, product requirements and handling training. Do not make manual lifting the default for people needing full assistance.

Wheelchair drive wheels and handrims are different. Rear wheels support and move the chair; the outer handrims are held for self-propulsion. Push handles are for helpers. Their presence does not establish the person’s propulsion ability.
Back support, seat, arm supports, leg supports and foot supports have different supporting roles. Identify front casters too. Foot supports are not steps for standing on during entry or exit.

Parking brakes differ from attendant brakes at the handles. Apply parking brakes when stationary, even unoccupied, and check tires and brake function before use. Low tire pressure can impair parking brakes. Lever position alone does not complete inspection.

A tipping lever helps raise or lower front wheels through trained operations suited to the model. Knowing its location does not authorize trying unfamiliar level changes. Check faults or handling uncertainty rather than continuing to use the equipment.

Distinguish words by action. Mobility changes location; a transfer changes the supporting place, such as bed to wheelchair. Sitting up raises the upper body from lying; rolling changes direction while lying. Being in bed differs from getting out of bed.

A slide sheet reduces friction, unlike a lifting device or a walker for walking support. For a senior pushcart, check model, ability and product purpose rather than assuming it replaces a walker or wheelchair. A white cane relates to visual impairment and should not be assumed equivalent to a weight-support cane selected by leg count.

In the Japanese braking expression, kakeru means applying the brake; tsuku in the cane expression means grounding it for support. Tsukamaru means holding a support, nigiru means gripping, and sasaeru means providing needed support to a body or object. Isolated word meanings do not establish the action without context.

Koekake means explaining or checking verbally with the person; yudo means guiding routes through a suitable method. Reading these terms does not remove explanation, consent, equipment checks or operating training.
[Learning example] Someone assumes more cane legs are best for everyone. A broad base is one feature; selection also depends on movement, setting, handling and instructed methods.

This teaches diagram and terminology meanings and reasons for assistance. Actual care follows condition, the individual care plan, product instructions and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar actions from words or pictures alone or record unchecked results.

kaigo-atomic-turning-sitting.heading: Distinguish conditions for rolling and sitting up
paragraphs: Before repositioning, check current condition, pain and movement range, explain the action and obtain consent. Prepare equipment, staffing, space and bed height. Do not continue for the schedule when the person is unwell; tell healthcare professionals or other appropriate recipients.

The textbook uses left-sided paralysis as one example of rolling with the affected side uppermost. Bending knees and other parts within available range compacts the body to make turning easier. Use personal abilities without pulling the affected arm to move the whole body.

After turning, the source example adjusts the pelvis/lower back backward and legs comfortably to establish stable side-lying support. Compacting for movement and widening support afterward serve different purposes. They are not contradictory instructions at the same moment. Specific positions and actions follow condition, the individual care plan and trained methods.

The sitting-up example moves from right side-lying, lowers both legs over the bed edge and uses the right elbow to raise the trunk into bed-edge sitting. It teaches coordination of legs, trunk and support, including the pictured right elbow. It does not require that elbow or identical arm use for everyone. Follow available strength, range, individual care plan and practical training.

Adjusting to a worker-suitable height aims to reduce lower-back strain. For bed-edge sitting, both soles need appropriate support such as the floor. Different task stages have different purposes; a convenient working height is not necessarily suitable for the person’s sitting.

After movement, check pain, well-being, dizziness, foot support and balance. Completed sitting-up movement does not establish stable sitting or readiness for standing or transfer. With unknown methods or changed condition, seek necessary help before starting the next action.

[Learning example] Someone applies the left-hemiplegia example’s knee and leg movements to a person with limited hip range. Diagnosis or diagram direction alone does not establish suitability. Check individual assessment, possible movements, plan and training. Understanding the diagram’s purpose differs from meeting conditions for use with this person.

This teaches diagram and terminology meanings and reasons for assistance. Actual care follows condition, the individual care plan, product instructions and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar actions from words or pictures alone or record unchecked results.

99.title: Read shaving and nail diagrams with their conditions
objectives: Distinguish illustrated movements from product-specific and personal conditions.
Check wishes and skin/nails and contact healthcare professionals about abnormalities.
99.context: Consider whether a remembered angle applies unchanged to another shaver type. Distinguish diagram understanding, product checks and personal consent.
99.artCaption: A clothing-choice scene prompts consideration of personal wishes in grooming too. This is not a shaving or nail-cutting technique diagram.

100.title: Understand why bed baths proceed area by area
objectives: Connect cleanliness, warmth, exposure scope and the area cleaned.
Distinguish movement direction from force and check drying and covering afterward.
100.context: Compare wetting everything before drying at the end with area-by-area care. Also check whole-body versus partial wishes.
100.artCaption: Prepare bed-bath supplies and surroundings. Water and towels alone do not establish temperature, cleanliness or completed assistance.

101.title: Consider mobility, ADL and IADL through daily purposes
objectives: Check independent parts and assistance needs for each activity.
101.context: Using someone who needs wheelchair help but manages money, distinguish mobility assistance from shopping decisions. Do not assume everything must be delegated to family.
101.artCaption: Discuss clothing actions the person does and needed help. One action does not establish other daily abilities.

102.title: Check position names and support locations
objectives: Distinguish position names/directions from repositioning actions.
Check comfort and support outcomes rather than cushion presence alone.
102.context: Consider whether a placed-pillow record proves comfort. Separate supported area, pressure, the person’s own words and actual checked results.
102.artCaption: Chairs and beds have different body-support surfaces and foot support. Check actual conditions as well as posture names.

103.title: Consider disuse and pressure risks from several perspectives
objectives: Distinguish inactivity-related changes from assumed causes.
Check pressure, skin, activity and nutrition as well as bedding wrinkles.
103.context: Consider checks needed after smoothing sheets for someone remaining in one posture. This does not diagnose every new symptom as disuse.
103.artCaption: Workers and healthcare professionals discuss posture, support surfaces and skin. The image cannot establish pressure-relief effectiveness.

104.title: Distinguish equipment features, components and purposes
objectives: Explain purposes and fit of canes, walkers and lifts.
Check wheelchair inspection and the distinction between mobility and transfer.
104.context: Consider whether a broader multipoint-cane base makes it best for everyone. Combine personal, environmental and product conditions.
104.artCaption: Staff check equipment purposes and suitable personal conditions. A lineup of aids does not establish safe use.

105.title: Read rolling and sitting-up examples with individual conditions
objectives: Separate facilitating movement from stabilizing posture afterward.
Check condition, available movements, foot support and post-assistance state.
105.context: Consider applying a left-hemiplegia example to someone with limited hip range. Individual assessment and trained methods are needed first.
105.artCaption: Check the individual care plan and roles before rolling or sitting up. Background conversation does not prove practical assistance is complete.

weekly-kaigo-atomic-case-grooming-figure.prompt: A remembered diagram angle is being applied to a differently structured shaver. What checks are needed?
options: All electric devices use identical angles and force.
Grooming wishes remove device-instruction checks.
Press firmly first and read instructions only if redness occurs.
Check model and instructions, skin and wishes, plan and consent before choosing the method.
rationales: The shared electric-shaver name does not remove product-specific structural and instruction checks.
Wishes and consent matter but are separate from checking appropriate equipment use.
Check a suitable method and condition before use, not after burdening skin.
This checks personal and product conditions rather than applying an example unconditionally.

weekly-kaigo-atomic-case-bed-wash-figure.prompt: A bed bath exposes and wets the whole body before drying at the end. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Correct wiping direction makes wet time and exposure irrelevant.
Bed-bath consent permits expanding a partial request to the whole body.
Check cleanliness and cleanser residue area by area, then dry and cover; check genital-care scope and clean–dirty separation too.
Cleanser residue is always cleaner left in place.
rationales: Warmth and privacy need attention separately from movement direction.
Check consent including scope; do not independently expand requested areas.
Avoid prolonged wet exposure while protecting warmth, clean skin and feelings of embarrassment.
Residue can burden skin and needs appropriate checking and removal.

weekly-kaigo-atomic-case-adl-iadl.prompt: The person needs wheelchair-mobility help but manages their budget. Which shopping support is appropriate?
options: Check wishes and managed tasks and assist where needed, such as mobility.
Families decide every purchase for wheelchair users.
Budgeting ability removes mobility-help needs.
Staff choose convenient stores and products and inform the person afterward.
rationales: This does not infer lost judgment or money management from mobility limits.
Mobility help and personal purchasing decisions are different abilities.
One IADL ability does not remove assistance needed for another action.
This replaces personal life choices with staff convenience.

weekly-kaigo-atomic-case-posture-names.prompt: A record says only ‘placed a pillow.’ Is comfortable positioning established?
options: Any pillow position removes pain.
Adding the name Fowler’s establishes checked support results.
A tidy appearance removes the need to ask sensations.
Not yet; check supported area and position, pressure, words and condition after adjustment.
rationales: Presence alone does not establish fit or absence of pain.
A posture name is not evidence of actual support or personal condition.
Appearance alone does not establish pain, breathing or sensation.
Placing an item and achieving suitable, comfortable support need separate checks.

weekly-kaigo-atomic-case-disuse.prompt: Sheets were smoothed for someone remaining in one posture. Which understanding of pressure-injury risk is appropriate?
options: No wrinkles makes prolonged pressure harmless.
Wrinkle reduction alone is insufficient; check pressure, sliding, skin, activity, nutrition and plan.
Do not report redness until a wound opens.
Diagnose all new dizziness and breathlessness as inactivity.
rationales: Smoothing does not remove sustained-pressure conditions.
Wrinkles are one factor; check others and personal condition too.
Report redness and other changes to healthcare professionals without waiting for wounds.
Even if inactivity can contribute, do not independently decide the cause of new symptoms.

weekly-kaigo-atomic-case-movement-device.prompt: Someone says a multipoint cane suits everyone better because of its broader base. Which correction is appropriate?
options: Base size is one feature; check abilities, surroundings, fit and instructed methods.
More legs removes the need to check handling.
Walkers and white canes have identical purposes and may be selected by shape.
Knowing cane types removes training and plan requirements.
rationales: Combine actual use conditions rather than ranking by one shape feature.
Safe handling matters; width alone does not establish fit.
Purposes and support conditions differ, beyond shape comparisons.
Names do not replace fit, operating training or individual care-plan checks.

weekly-kaigo-atomic-case-turning-sitting.prompt: A left-hemiplegia example is being applied unchanged to someone with limited hip range. What is appropriate?
options: The same posture name permits identical motion regardless of joint limits.
Memorized order removes explanation and consent.
Check individual assessment, range, plan and trained method rather than directly applying the example.
After sitting up, immediately stand without checking feet or dizziness.
rationales: Identical labels still require individual range and method checks.
Procedure knowledge does not replace understanding and consent.
A conditional example cannot prescribe the same method under different joint conditions.
Completed sitting-up movement differs from stable sitting; check before the next action.
